strengths: The introduction of multi-modal panoramic representations as an intermediate 2D-3D interface is highly effective. It preserves a 360-degree field of view to capture complex, long-range spatial relationships, which is a major advantage over pinhole-based approaches.
The paper achieves state-of-the-art or top-performing results on major benchmarks like ScanRefer and Nr3D, especially on human-annotated splits where linguistic diversity is high.

Excellent generalization analysis on unseen 3D datasets (ARKitScenes, 3RScan) and under extreme linguistic perturbations (masking nouns, using affordances), demonstrating the robustness of using a 2D VLM-based panoramic bridge over direct 3D training.
The paper is very well-written and thoroughly ablated, providing useful insights into camera placement scoring, loss objectives (like EMD), and the comparison between Mesh vs. 3DGS representations.
weaknesses: High computational cost and latency: The online inference takes ~3.3 seconds per query, relying on a 17B parameter VLM (CogVLM-17B) run multiple times (9.6 forward passes on average) per scene, plus SAM for segmentation. This limits its applicability in real-time robotic systems.

Heavy dependency on complex, multi-stage preprocessing pipelines, including RANSAC floor estimation, multi-view feature projection to construct a 3D semantic field, and equirectangular depth/feature rendering.

The framework assumes a pre-reconstructed, static 3D scene (either a clean mesh or a pre-trained Gaussian Splat) to select camera views and render panoramas, which is less feasible for active, on-the-fly exploration where 3D geometry is partial and noisy.

strengths: The choice of panoramic (360-degree field of view) equirectangular renderings as an intermediate 2D-3D interface is highly intuitive and elegant. It effectively solves the narrow field-of-view and view-selection limitations of standard pinhole-based approaches, preserving spatial relationships within a single image context.

The paper introduces a well-designed structure-aware camera placement strategy that optimizes spatial coverage, maintains distance from obstacles, and leverages the capture trajectory to ensure high-quality panoramic renderings.

Strong experimental performance on ScanRefer and Nr3D. The generalization experiments on unseen environments (ARKitScenes, 3RScan) and language perturbations (such as removing explicit target class names) are outstanding and demonstrate that the model actually performs contextual and spatial reasoning rather than simple lexical matching.

Excellent ablation studies and supplementary materials that thoroughly dissect the system's components, including camera placement factors, training objectives (EMD loss, Geometric QA), and representation type (Mesh vs. 3DGS).
weaknesses: The framework has high computational and latency overhead. Running a 17B parameter model (CogVLM) multiple times (averaging 9.6 forward passes per query due to multiple camera views and test-time augmentation) results in an online runtime of 3.3 seconds on an A100. This is considerably slower and more resource-intensive than traditional end-to-end 3D visual grounding methods.

The pipeline relies heavily on accurate multi-modal inputs, including pre-computed camera trajectories, camera poses, and dense geometry (meshes or 3DGS). If the underlying 3D reconstruction is incomplete or noisy, or if camera trajectories are unavailable, the camera placement and multi-view feature fusion components may experience performance degradation.

The multi-stage design is somewhat complex, involving a sequence of non-differentiable steps: RANSAC floor estimation, greedy camera placement, offline 3D semantic field projection, 2D VLM inference, SAM-based segmentation, and visibility-aware aggregation.

strengths: Innovative use of multi-modal panoramic representations (RGB, range, and multi-view fused semantics) as a 2D-3D bridge. This effectively addresses the narrow field-of-view and spatial relationship preservation limitations of standard pinhole rendering while staying fully compatible with 2D VLMs.

Strong state-of-the-art results on widely used 3DVG benchmarks, showing clear gains in the challenging human-annotated Nr3D (+4.7% over previous state-of-the-art) and ScanRefer (+1.4% overall in the single-dataset setup).

Excellent robustness and generalization capabilities, demonstrated through cross-dataset transfer (ARKitScenes, 3RScan) and complex linguistic perturbations (e.g., LLaMA-generated noun masking and affordance queries), where it significantly outperforms existing baselines.

Comprehensive and systematic ablation studies in both the main text and supplementary material, validating the design choices for camera placement, input modalities, auxiliary geometric QA, and the EMD loss formulation.
weaknesses: High computational complexity and latency: The system relies on a heavy 17B parameter VLM (CogVLM). Processing multiple panoramic viewpoints with test-time augmentations (9.6 forward passes per query on average) leads to an online query latency of approximately 3.3 seconds on a high-end NVIDIA A100 GPU, limiting real-time robotics or AR applications.

Complex multi-stage pipeline: The approach consists of several disparate modules, including floor plane estimation, greedy camera planning, multi-modal rendering, VLM processing, SAM mask-to-3D lifting, cross-view consistency selection, and 3D bounding box fitting. This complexity increases potential points of failure and introduces many hyperparameters.

Heavy dependency on high-quality 3D reconstructions and camera trajectories: As discussed in the paper, rendering artifacts from reconstructed representations (like 3DGS) can degrade the feature adapters' inputs and lower overall accuracy compared to using clean mesh models.

strengths: A well-motivated and novel 2D-3D interface using panoramic scene representations (360-degree FOV) for 3D Visual Grounding, which effectively resolves the field-of-view limits and view-selection issues inherent in pinhole camera approaches.

Well-designed technical components, including: (1) an elegant greedy structure-aware camera placement algorithm; (2) multi-modal feature adapters injecting geometry and multi-view semantic features into appropriate VLM layers; and (3) a distance-aware Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) loss to regularize autoregressive bounding box coordinate predictions.

State-of-the-art results on ScanRefer and Nr3D, outperforming existing 3D-based and VLM-based baselines. Notably, the zero-shot performance with CogVLM-17B even outperforms significantly larger models like GPT-4V and Qwen2-VL-72B.

Comprehensive and extensive evaluations including cross-dataset generalization (on ARKitScenes and 3RScan), linguistic robustness analysis (using LLaMA-generated perturbations), and a practical demonstration of real-world deployment on a self-captured iPhone video with 3DGS.

The manuscript is extremely well-written, and the supplementary material provides thorough ablation studies regarding camera placement, layer placement probing, test-time rotation augmentation, and resource usage.
weaknesses: High pipeline complexity: The method is a multi-stage approach involving RANSAC-based floor estimation, viewpoint selection, multi-modal rendering, 2D VLM inference, 2D SAM segmentation, and 3D lifting/aggregation. This makes it less unified and more complex than end-to-end 3D-based models.

Inference latency: Due to the autoregressive VLM forward passes (especially with the default CogVLM-17B) and multiple yaw rotations, the online query latency is relatively high (3.30s per query) compared to fully feed-forward 3D methods.

Dependence on 3D reconstruction: The performance is tightly coupled with the quality of the underlying 3D mesh or 3D Gaussian Splatting. Floater artifacts or incomplete reconstructions in sparsely scanned regions can directly degrade the rendering and lead to VLM localization errors.

strengths: Innovative intermediate representation: Proposing panoramic renderings as a 2D-3D interface is a highly intuitive and effective way to preserve scene-wide spatial context while maintaining compatibility with powerful pretrained 2D VLMs.
Excellent performance: PanoGrounder achieves state-of-the-art results on ScanRefer and Nr3D, particularly excelling in complex multi-object queries and challenging relational cases.

Linguistic and cross-dataset robustness: The model exhibits superior generalization compared to existing baselines when evaluated on unseen 3D datasets (ARKitScenes, 3RScan) and under diverse textual perturbations (such as when the target object noun is masked out).

Thorough evaluation and design validation: The paper is backed by extensive ablation studies (covering camera placement, input modalities, VLM backbones, and rendering settings) and includes a practical demonstration on real-world, self-captured data.
weaknesses: Dependence on 3D reconstruction quality: Since the approach relies on rendering panoramas from meshes or 3D Gaussian Splatting, severe reconstruction noise or incomplete geometry can directly degrade VLM performance.

Inference latency: Processing multiple panoramic views (along with test-time yaw rotations) on large VLMs (like CogVLM-17B) introduces non-negligible computational overhead, although the authors partially address this with smaller backbones like Qwen2.5-VL-3B.

Equirectangular distortion: Standard 2D VLMs are pretrained on perspective images, and the equirectangular projection used for panoramas introduces severe distortion, particularly at high or low elevation angles.

strengths: The proposed panoramic representation is an elegant and effective intermediate bridge between 2D VLMs and 3D scenes, combining a holistic 360-degree field of view with VLM compatibility.
The design of the structure-aware camera placement strategy is well-reasoned and thoroughly ablated, demonstrating that it successfully covers the scene with very few viewpoints (2.4 on average).

The integration of multi-modal features (geometric and semantic) via lightweight zero-initialized adapters and the use of the EMD loss for numeric coordinate regression are technically sound and show clear benefits.

The paper provides an exceptionally comprehensive evaluation, showing state-of-the-art performance on Nr3D, Sr3D, and ScanRefer, alongside impressive results in cross-dataset generalization and text robustness.

The supplementary material is exceptionally detailed, featuring deep-dive studies on camera selection factors, backbone scalability, real-world deployment on self-captured scenes, and layer-probing analyses.
weaknesses: The pipeline relies heavily on high-quality 3D reconstructions (meshes or 3DGS), which require significant offline preprocessing time (e.g., COLMAP and 3DGS training).
Inference latency is relatively high due to multiple VLM forward passes (averaging 9.6 passes per query with yaw rotations), which might limit its real-time applicability in robotics.
The model is dependent on external tools like SAM for mask-to-3D lifting, making the final 3D prediction quality susceptible to error propagation from the 2D segmenter.
